::: {.callout-note}
Written with the ADaM (F3 day 9) and completed with the clinical study report, after the
database lock (tag `dblock-301`). The reviewer then authorised the unblinding
(`docs/unblind/unblind-301.yml`, ADR 0032). The counts here are of the locked data and do not
depend on the arms. The structure follows the PHUSE ADRG template.
The data are simulated and the sponsor is fictional.
:::

## 1. Introduction

The package holds the ADaM datasets of FJF-2026-301. They are SAS transport v5 files with
Parquet copies, described by `define.xml` (Define-XML 2.1). Standards: ADaMIG 1.3, CDISC ADaM
terminology 2024-03-29. Each dataset is derived from the SDTM package (`../sdtm`) by the
programs in `studies/301/adam`, following the specification `docs/specs/adam-301.yml` and the
frozen SAP (tag `sap-301-v1.0`). Analysis results metadata and value-level metadata are not in
the define.xml; the outputs specification (`docs/sap/fjf-2026-301-outputs.yml`) links each
table and figure to the variables it uses.

## 2. Protocol description

See the cSDRG, section 2. The analysis sets are those of the SAP:

| Set | Flag | Definition | Patients |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: |
| Full analysis | FASFL | Randomised | 300 |
| Safety | SAFFL | Randomised and dosed; by treatment taken | 300 |
| Per protocol | PPROTFL | FAS, compliance ≥ 80%, week-26 HbA1c on treatment and before rescue | 214 |

Protocol deviations are not collected in this study, so no patient is excluded from the
per-protocol set for a deviation.

## 3. Analysis considerations

- **Study day** counts from randomisation (day 1, no day 0), as the SAP says. The SDTM --DY
  variables count from the first dose, so ADY and --DY can differ.
- **Visit windows** (ADEFF): each value goes to the nearest scheduled visit by study day
  (target 7 × week + 1). Window boundaries are the midpoints between targets, and a value
  exactly on a midpoint goes to the earlier visit. The last window ends half the previous gap
  after its target. Within a window, the closest value is selected (ANL01FL), the later one on
  a tie. Body weight is windowed with the same rule at its scheduled visits (weeks 12 and 26).
- **Missing visits** are records with DTYPE = PHANTOM: AVAL and CHG are empty, and the
  on-treatment and pre-rescue flags are judged at the target day. The multiple-imputation
  models then see every scheduled visit.
- **Baselines**: for efficacy, the last value on or before randomisation, with a missing
  HbA1c baseline replaced by the stratum mean (BIMPFL; none). For safety
  (ADLB, ADVS), the last value on or before the first dose.
- **Intercurrent events**:
  - ONTRTFL marks values on treatment (up to 7 days after the last dose).
  - PRERESFL marks values on or before the first rescue dose.
  - ANL02FL selects the values of the hypothetical estimand.
  - Record-level flags are Y or empty.
- **Treatment-emergent AEs**: onset on or after the first dose and up to 14 days after the
  last. Partial start dates (17) are imputed to the first dose when the period contains it
  and the event did not end before it; otherwise to the first day of the period (ASTDTF).
- **Worst laboratory value** (WORSTFL): the on-treatment value furthest outside its range, as
  a multiple of the limit crossed; if none is outside, the last on treatment. 33 patients
  stopped treatment before week 12, the first chemistry visit after baseline, so they have no
  worst value for the chemistry tests.
- **Blinding**: the database is locked and the reviewer authorised the unblinding (ADR 0032).
  The treatment variables (TRT01P, TRT01A, TRTP, TRTA and their numeric codes) are the real
  ones. Before the unblinding the same programs ran on a dummy assignment (ADR 0027).
- **Vital signs outside limits** (ADVS.CRIT1FL, CRIT2FL): the SAP names them but does not
  give them. The reviewer set them before the lock: systolic ≥ 160 or ≤ 90 mmHg, diastolic
  ≥ 100 or ≤ 50 mmHg, pulse ≥ 120 or ≤ 50 beats/min, weight ±7% from baseline (ADR 0028).
- **Missing AE severity** counts as severe in ASEV, flagged by ASEVIMFL (CR09; 4 events).
- **Last dose**: the disposition page's last-dose date is the end of treatment; for 129
  patients whose last bottle ends earlier, that bottle runs until it (CR10). This enters
  compliance.
- **ECG**: the protocol schedules a 12-lead ECG at screening and week 26, but the ECG is not
  in the study database (no EG domain), so there is no ECG analysis dataset. Table 14.3.5
  says so.

## 4. Data conformance

See `studies/301/conformance.md`, section *Conformance of the ADaM*. P21 (ADaM-IG 1.3, FDA)
has no rejects. Two items are explained there: there are no MedDRA codes (licence), and the
traceability rules are not run by P21. A second programming (`qc/301/adam_qc.R`) agrees with
production on all datasets.

## 5. Datasets

| Dataset | Class | Records | Key variables |
| --- | --- | ---: | --- |
| ADSL | Subject level | 300 | analysis sets, treatment dates, intercurrent-event dates, baselines |
| ADEFF | BDS | HbA1c and weight by analysis visit | PARAMCD, AVISITN, ANL01FL, ANL02FL, CRIT1FL |
| ADTTE | BDS | 600 | TTRESC (FAS), TTHYPO23 (SAF) |
| ADEX | Other | 300 | TRTDURD, TRTDURY, COMPLPCT |
| ADAE | OCCDS | 400 | TRTEMFL, ASTDT, ASTDTF, ASEV |
| ADHYPO | OCCDS | 45 | HYPOLVL, ONTRTFL, PRERESFL |
| ADLB | BDS | 10,808 | BASE, BNRIND, ANRIND, WORSTFL |
| ADVS | BDS | 9,848 | BASE, CHG, PCHG, ANL01FL, CRIT1FL, CRIT2FL |

## 6. Decisions taken before the lock

All are listed in ADR 0028, with who took them. CDISC CORE was run on SDTM (`conformance.md`);
it has no published ADaM rules.

## 7. Outputs and their programs

Each table and figure is listed in `docs/sap/fjf-2026-301-outputs.yml` with the SAP item it
implements, the ADaM variables it reads and its program (`studies/301/tlf/`). A second
programming of the tables (`qc/301/tlf_qc.R`) agrees with production cell by cell. The
clinical study report (`studies/301/csr.qmd`) embeds the outputs the pipeline makes.
